newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON DSM H1 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON DSM H1 RESULTS.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV on Wednesday reported 1997 first-half net profit up 13 percent at 465 million guilders and predicted "clearly higher" earnings for the full year.
Below is a selection of analysts' comments:

"These results are at the lower end of market expectations. Turnover rose nicely in the various divisions, notably in hydrocarbons/polymers. This underlines the healthy economic growth in Europe, and consequent growth in demand. But the margin development was disappointing, especially in base and fine chemicals. Prospects for 1997 seem good, but additional capacity will lead to overcapacity in hydrocarbons and polymers from the fourth quarter and it will be felt in the margins in 1998. We maintain our hold rating for DSM."

"The figures are somewhat weak, but there's a significant increase in turnover. I had feared the results of base chemicals would be disappointing, but not to such a level. I think the fertilisers business might have pressured the division."

"I thought the results were a little disappointing, especially the developments in industrial and fine chemicals. The forecast for the second half year was quite new and they might just exceed our estimates for the full year. But in general we think the outlook for DSM in the next two years is not so good and our recommendation remains at Underperformer."
